A_target.statement: In a [[Definition:Dataflow Analysis|dataflow analysis]] over a lattice $L$ of finite height, with [[Definition:Increasing Mapping|monotone]] transfer functions, the iterative algorithm, which starts from $\bot$ at every program point and re-applies the equations until nothing changes, terminates and returns the least solution of the dataflow equations.

B_source.statement:
Let $D$ be a [[Definition:Complete Partial Order|complete partial order]] with bottom and $F: D \to D$ [[Definition:Scott-Continuous Mapping|Scott-continuous]].
Then $\displaystyle \bigsqcup_n \map {F^n} \bot$ is the least fixed point of $F$.

substitutions.the CPO: the product lattice L^N over the N program points
substitutions.the map F: simultaneous application of all dataflow equations

derived.the Kleene chain: the successive rounds of the iterative algorithm

object_map.reformulation: Encode the dataflow equations as one monotone map on a product lattice and iterate it from the bottom element.

validity_conditions: Finite height makes every increasing chain stabilize, so monotone maps are continuous and the iteration terminates.
Worklist orders reach the same least fixed point, as long as every equation is eventually re-evaluated.
proof_plan: With program points $1, \ldots, N$, the equations $x_i = \map {f_i} {\bigsqcup_{j \in \map {\operatorname {pred} } i} x_j}$ define a monotone map $F$ on $L^N$.

$L^N$ has finite height $N h$, where $h$ is the height of $L$.
Hence every increasing chain stabilizes, and a monotone $F$ is Scott-continuous.
The chain $\map {F^n} \bot$ is increasing, so it stabilizes after at most $N h$ rounds, at a fixed point.

By the source result, this fixed point is the least solution of the equations, which is what the iterative algorithm returns.
{{qed}}
